name: Mozilla Firefox
about: Fast, privacy-minded browser from the non-profit Mozilla Foundation. Built on its own Gecko engine, with strong tracking protection, container tabs and a huge extension library.

name: Brave
about: Chromium-based browser that blocks ads and trackers by default with its built-in Shields. Works with Chrome extensions and adds optional rewards and VPN features.

name: Google Chrome
about: Google's widely used browser, with fast page loading, Google account sync and the largest extension ecosystem. Freeware, but the full build is not open source.

name: Mozilla Thunderbird
about: Free email client with calendar, contacts and tasks. Supports multiple accounts, IMAP, POP and Exchange, and add-ons for extra features.

name: Signal
about: End-to-end encrypted messenger for text, voice and video, run by the non-profit Signal Foundation. Collects almost no metadata and is open source.

name: Discord
about: Chat platform for communities and friends, with text channels, voice rooms, screen sharing and bots. The client is proprietary but free to use.

name: Telegram Desktop
about: Official desktop client for the Telegram messenger. Fast, syncs across devices and supports large groups, channels and bots. The client is open source; the servers are not.

name: Element
about: Secure team and personal chat built on the open Matrix protocol. Supports encrypted rooms, bridges to other chat networks and self-hosted servers.

name: VLC media player
about: The classic cross-platform player that handles almost any video, audio or streaming format without extra codecs. Also converts and streams media.

name: OBS Studio
about: Free tool for screen recording and live streaming. Compose scenes from windows, cameras and audio sources and stream to Twitch, YouTube and others.

name: Audacity
about: Popular multi-track audio editor and recorder. Good for podcasts, cleaning up noise, cutting clips and applying effects.

name: HandBrake
about: Open-source video transcoder. Converts videos between formats with presets for phones, TVs and web, and offers fine control over quality and size.

name: Kdenlive
about: Full-featured multi-track video editor from the KDE community. Includes effects, titling, proxy editing and a flexible timeline.

name: Shotcut
about: Cross-platform video editor with a wide range of formats, filters and 4K support. Straightforward to learn and runs from a modest PC.

name: Blender
about: Complete 3D creation suite for modeling, sculpting, animation, rendering, VFX and video editing. Used from hobby projects to feature films.

name: GIMP
about: Powerful free image editor for photo retouching, compositing and graphic design. A long-standing open-source alternative to Photoshop.

name: Krita
about: Painting program built for illustrators, concept artists and comic creators. Offers brush engines, layers, animation tools and a pen-tablet-friendly interface.

name: Inkscape
about: Professional vector graphics editor using the SVG format. Great for logos, icons, posters and technical illustration.

name: darktable
about: Open-source photography workflow app and RAW developer. Manage a photo library and edit non-destructively with masks and color tools.

name: 7-Zip
about: Lightweight file archiver with a high compression ratio. Opens ZIP, RAR, TAR and many other formats, and creates its own 7z archives.

name: PeaZip
about: Free archive manager with a friendly interface. Handles many formats, supports encryption and can split or convert archives.

name: ShareX
about: Feature-rich screenshot and screen-recording tool. Capture regions or scrolling pages, annotate, and upload to many services automatically.

name: Microsoft PowerToys
about: A set of Microsoft utilities for power users, including FancyZones window layouts, a quick launcher, a color picker, bulk file renamer and more.

name: Everything
about: Finds files and folders on your PC almost instantly by name. Much faster than the built-in search because it indexes the file system directly.

name: WinDirStat
about: Shows disk usage as a colorful treemap so you can quickly see which files and folders are taking up the most space.

name: Notepad++
about: Fast, lightweight text and source-code editor with tabs, syntax highlighting for many languages, macros and plugins.

name: LibreOffice
about: Full office suite with Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw and Base. Opens and saves Microsoft Office files and is free for any use.

name: SumatraPDF
about: Very small and fast reader for PDF, ePub, MOBI, comics and more. Starts instantly and has a minimal, distraction-free interface.

name: PDF24 Creator
about: Free PDF toolbox that installs a virtual printer to create PDFs from any app, plus tools to merge, split, compress and convert.

name: KeePassXC
about: Offline password manager that keeps your encrypted database in a local file. Includes a TOTP generator and browser integration.

name: Bitwarden
about: Open-source password manager with cloud sync, browser autofill and an optional self-hosted server. A generous free tier covers most users.

name: VeraCrypt
about: Disk encryption software that creates encrypted containers or encrypts whole partitions. A well-known successor to TrueCrypt.

name: Cryptomator
about: Encrypts files before they reach your cloud storage. Creates a virtual drive, so it works with Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive and others.

name: WireGuard
about: Official WireGuard client for Windows. A fast, modern VPN protocol with a small codebase that is easy to audit and configure.

name: Syncthing
about: Continuous peer-to-peer file synchronization between your devices. No cloud server involved, and all traffic is encrypted.

name: Git
about: The standard distributed version-control system. Track changes, branch and collaborate on code or any text files.

name: Visual Studio Code
about: Microsoft's popular, extensible code editor with debugging, Git integration and thousands of extensions. Built from open source code but distributed under a proprietary license.

name: VSCodium
about: Community build of VS Code from the open-source code, without Microsoft branding or telemetry. Uses the Open VSX extension registry.

name: Python 3
about: The Python language and interpreter. Popular for scripting, automation, data science and web development. Pinned to a specific minor version in this catalog.

name: Node.js LTS
about: JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine, used to build servers, tools and apps. The LTS release gets long-term support and is the safest choice.

name: GitHub Desktop
about: Graphical Git client from GitHub. Simplifies cloning, committing, branching and opening pull requests without using the command line.

name: Wireshark
about: The world's leading network protocol analyzer. Capture traffic and inspect it in detail to troubleshoot or learn how protocols work.

name: DBeaver Community
about: Universal database tool with a SQL editor and data viewer. Supports many databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite and more.

name: Docker Desktop
about: Run containers on your PC with a graphical dashboard, Docker Engine and Kubernetes. Free for personal use and small businesses; larger companies need a paid plan.
license: Free for some use; terms apply

name: Steam
about: Valve's PC game store and launcher, with a huge library, cloud saves, Workshop mods and community features.

name: Prism Launcher
about: Minecraft launcher that manages multiple separate instances, mod loaders and modpacks without them interfering with each other.

name: Heroic Games Launcher
description: Alternative Epic, GOG and Amazon launcher
about: Open-source launcher for your Epic Games, GOG and Amazon Games libraries, with a clean interface and Wine/Proton options.

name: Spotify
about: Desktop app for streaming music and podcasts. Free with ads, or subscribe for ad-free listening and offline downloads.

name: qBittorrent
about: Free, ad-free BitTorrent client with a search plugin, RSS support and a web interface. A popular open-source alternative to uTorrent.

name: Mozilla Firefox ESR
about: Firefox Extended Support Release. Gets security fixes but feature changes arrive more slowly, which suits organisations and anyone who prefers stability.

name: Microsoft Edge
about: Microsoft's Chromium-based browser, built into Windows. Supports Chrome extensions and offers vertical tabs, collections and Microsoft account sync.

name: Opera
about: Chromium-based browser with a built-in VPN proxy, ad blocker and sidebar messengers. Good for people who like extra built-in features.

name: Vivaldi
about: Highly customizable Chromium-based browser with tab stacking, built-in notes, mail and calendar, and detailed interface options.

name: Tor Browser
about: Browser that routes traffic through the Tor network to hide your location and resist tracking. Suitable for privacy and censorship circumvention.
